messages:
alex: heads-up — we're getting a customer escalation (TKT-2481) about a sudden p99 tail spike on /v1/generate since yesterday's batching config push. p50 unchanged (~60ms) but p95 went from 120ms -> 190ms and p99 from ~800ms -> ~1.2s. saw this in us-west and eu-west.
mira: ack. which config change landed? last change was the continuous-batcher default timeout bump from 12ms -> 40ms to help throughput during cold tails.
alex: yes that commit: deploy/1762089001 — flagged increase of continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms to 40. Also increased max_batch_size for small models to 64.
julian: that would explain more waiting for batches to fill. under low QPS the batcher holds requests until timeout or size so p99 can blow up. do we have traces for affected requests?
sre-bot: incident.created TKT-2481: "p99 regression on /v1/generate after batching config change" — assigned to eng-runtime.
alex: attaching quick logs snippet from one host (trimmed):

```
[2026-02-28T18:02:11Z] req_id=xyz123 model=redwood-1 seq=64 size=280 tokens waiting_for_batch=true wait_ms=38 dispatched_at=2026-02-28T18:02:11.038Z latency_total_ms=1220
[2026-02-28T18:02:11Z] req_id=abc987 model=redwood-1 seq=16 size=64 waiting_for_batch=false dispatched_at=2026-02-28T18:02:11.020Z latency_total_ms=85
```

alex: note waiting_for_batch=true line — long wait_ms ~38ms tends to add up to p99.
mira: repro steps I'd use:
1) hit /v1/generate with variable seq lengths, low concurrency (QPS ~3-5) to mimic customer traffic.
2) send single requests with small payloads spaced 50ms apart to see if batcher groups them and waits.
3) capture X-Req-Id and service logs.

curl example to reproduce (basic):
```
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello","max_tokens":10}' & sleep 0.05; done
```

julian: quick mitigation options:
- reduce continuous_batcher.batch_timeout_ms back to 12 (rollback) — fastest.
- add an override: for SLO-critical customers route to a low-latency pool with batch_timeout_ms=6.
- enable adaptive dispatch: if queue depth < 3 dispatch immediately.
- cap max_batch_size to 16 for small-seq models.

support_lead: customer needs immediate workaround. can we do a targeted rollback on their dedicated pool?
ingrid: yes we can patch routing rules for that tenant to use low-latency profile. ops can flip a per-tenant flag within 5 minutes.
mira: before rollback let's validate — can we run a canary change on a single node? idea: change batch_timeout to 8ms on 1 host, run the curl loop and compare p99.
julian: agreed. I'll coordinate a quick canary on runtime-staging-3 and post metrics.

[10 minutes later]
julian: canary results: batch_timeout=8ms -> p95 ~130ms, p99 ~420ms. baseline (40ms) -> p95 190ms, p99 ~1.2s. throughput minor dip ~3%. logs show fewer waiting_for_batch=true events.
alex: nice. ops: can we stage a tenant-specific override now? support_lead the customer accepted a temporary routing change.
ops: scheduling change: routing rule set for tenant=acme-corp -> low_latency_profile applied at 2026-03-02T14:07:12Z (rolled to 3 nodes). monitoring: p99 for the tenant dropped from 1.1s -> 360ms within 10 minutes.
support_lead: customer confirmed improved experience and closed their escalated complaint for now but asked for a long-term fix.
mira: long-term fixes proposal:
- implement dynamic batch_timeout that shrinks based on observed request inter-arrival for each model/route.
- add heuristic to dispatch small-requests immediately if queue depth < 2.
- expose per-tenant SLO tags so customers can opt into low-latency pools.
- add automated regression alert if p95 or p99 jumps >30% after config deploy.

alex: action items:
- julian: prepare PR to add queue-depth immediate-dispatch heuristic (ETA 2w).
- eng-runtime: add a deploy gate to warn when batch_timeout_ms increases >10ms for stable models (owner: mira, ETA 1w).
- ops: keep per-tenant override playbook updated and add a runbook snippet (owner: ingrid, ETA 3d).
- support_lead: follow up with customer and convert to post-incident notes (owner: support_lead, ETA today).

ingrid: FYI — I'll document the quick rollback steps in ops-runbook under continuous-batcher and add the canary commands.

mira: closing loop: we should ship a small hotfix to lower default batch_timeout for small models and add a telemetry tag to trace waiting_for_batch boolean on spans. will open a ticket for infra instrumentation.

alex: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for postmortem notes; will file a short postmortem after we confirm the long-term changes.
